Documentation → Administration → Settings → Backup Server

Backup Server settings

The external SFTP server that device config backups, SATOM's own system bundles, archived firmware and off-box SoT data are copied to — plus the hour the system bundle is written and how many bundles stay on the node.

👤 ForAdministratorAdvanced user
🔑 Permissionsusers.manage
📍 WhereSettings → Source of Truth & Backup → Backup Server (URL /settings/#tab-backupsrv)

What is it?#

The Backup Server tab configures the SFTP box that several separate streams are copied to. It is a destination, not an authority: nothing stored there decides what a device is configured to do — that is the Configuration SoT. The same tab sets when this node writes its own system bundle and how many bundles it keeps locally.

What does it do?#

Stream Written by Path field
Device config backups the appliances themselves, on their own schedule (config system backup); SATOM reads, indexes and diffs them Config backups path
System bundles this node's scheduled system_backup action (PostgreSQL dump + JSON tree + SoT blobs), and a manual Create backup now on System backup when its push box is ticked System bundles path
Firmware archive images archived when they leave local storage Firmware archive path
SoT change-log archive the Configuration SoT evacuation <System bundles path>/sot-log/

ℹ️Note

Changed in 2.11.0: a manual bundle from System backup can now be pushed to this server, and messages that point here name the tab as Settings → Source of Truth & Backup → Backup Server.

The System Backup page that lists and restores bundles is documented in System backup.

Requirements#

  • users.manage.
  • An SFTP account on the backup server. Paths are as seen inside the SFTP session (the server typically chroots the backup user).

Permissions#

🔑Permission

Every action on this tab (POST /settings/backup-server, /backup-server/test, /backup-server/schedule, /backup-server/bundle-retention, /backup-server/bundle-evict) requires users.manage. Without it the group is not shown and direct calls return 403.

How to use#

Configure the server#

  1. Open Settings → Source of Truth & Backup → Backup Server.
  2. Fill Host, Port, Username, Password and the three paths.
  3. Click Save backup server settings — "Backup server settings saved."
  4. Click Test connection. On success it shows connected to <host>:<port> — N device folder(s) under <config path>, M file(s) under <firmware path>.

❗Important — Test uses the saved values

Test connection reads the stored settings, not the values currently typed in the form, and lists only the config-backups and firmware paths. Save first, then test.

Set the bundle hour#

  1. In System bundle schedule, set Daily, at (HH:MM). The time is wall-clock in the console timezone printed under the field (set on General).
  2. Click Save bundle schedule. The flash reads "System bundles are now written at HH:MM <timezone>." or, if nothing was scheduled, "Created a nightly system backup at HH:MM <timezone>."

Set local bundle retention#

  1. In Local bundle retention, set Bundles kept on this node.
  2. Click Save bundle retention. The flash reads "System bundles: keeping N on this node after a verified upload. …"
  3. To apply it immediately, click Evict verified bundles now in Apply bundle retention now.

Configuration#

Field Description Required Example
Host SFTP server name or address. The server counts as configured only when Host and Username are set. Yes backup.example.com
Port Default 22; clamped to 1–65535, invalid → 22. No 22
Username SFTP user. Yes satom-backup
Password Stored Fernet-encrypted, never shown back. Leave blank to keep the current one (placeholder Leave blank to keep current). First time —
Config backups path One sub-folder per appliance, named as the device is named in SATOM. Default /configs. No /configs
Firmware archive path Default /firmware. No /firmware
System bundles path Default /system. Also the parent of the SoT change-log archive (sot-log/). No /system
Daily, at Hour of the daily system_backup run, HH:MM in the console timezone. Default 01:30. An unparseable value keeps the hour already in force. Disabled when the bundle runs on a non-daily schedule. No 02:15
Bundles kept on this node Bundles kept locally after a size-verified upload. Default 0 (keep none), range 0–365. Zero is a real value here; the page says whether it is configured on this node or not configured; the default is in effect. No 0

Example#

🧪Example — Keep one local bundle for fast restores

Set Bundles kept on this node to 1 and save. After the next successful upload, all but the newest verified bundle are removed locally. A bundle the server does not hold at the same size is always kept, whatever the number says.

Result#

  • Credentials and paths are stored in app_settings (backup_server.config, password encrypted); audit entry settings.backup_server.
  • Save bundle schedule edits (or creates, enabled with catch-up) the daily system_backup scheduled action with push_server on, recomputes its next run and writes settings.system_backup_schedule. The card shows the driving action, its last status and next run in UTC, and DISABLED, so this node is writing no bundles at all right now when the row is off.
  • Retention runs automatically after every successful upload; Evict verified bundles now runs it on demand and uploads nothing.
  • A run whose upload fails still leaves a local bundle — then the local copy is the only copy.

Troubleshooting#

"backup server not configured (Settings → Source of Truth & Backup → Backup Server)"#

Possible causes — Host or Username is empty in the saved settings.

Solution — fill both on this tab and click Save backup server settings before testing.

Test connection fails with an authentication or socket error#

Possible causes — wrong password, port, or firewall between the node and the server; the config or firmware path does not exist inside the chroot.

Solution 1. Correct and save the values (a blank password keeps the stored one). 2. Make sure both Config backups path and Firmware archive path exist on the server.

Verification — the green line lists the device folders and firmware files found.

"This node backs up on a … schedule, which one hour cannot express — change it in Automation rather than adding a second nightly bundle."#

Possible causes — the existing system_backup row is weekly, interval or another non-daily kind. The field is disabled and the save is refused so that no second bundle is scheduled.

Solution — edit the row in Scheduled actions, or change it to a daily schedule there.

"Nothing removed. N kept by policy, M not verified on the backup server (K bundle(s) known off-box)."#

Possible causes — bundles were never uploaded, or the server copy has a different size.

Solution — check the upload status of the latest system_backup run; fix the credentials and let the next run upload.

An empty config-backups folder#

Possible causes — the appliance is not pushing its own backups. SATOM does not author device backups; it can report the gap but not fill it.

Solution — configure the scheduled backup on the appliance (see Backups).

Advanced#

Advanced Internals
  • Bundle eviction deletes a local bundle only when the server listing shows it at the same size; downloading or restoring an off-box bundle fetches it back first (see System backup).
  • When the hour field creates the schedule, the new action is named Nightly system backup (Postgres + JSON); rename it in Automation if you like.
  • The three save buttons post to separate endpoints on purpose, so changing the hour or the retention never rewrites the SFTP credentials.
